recipes.name: Tom's Sweet Pimento Cheese
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup creamy salad dressing (such as Miracle Whip®)

steps.text: Beat the cream cheese and Cheddar cheese together with an electric mixer in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in the salad dressing, garlic salt, sugar, and pickle juice, scraping down the sides of the mixing bowl. Stir in the pickle relish and pimentos. Refrigerate for at least one hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Tom's Sweet Pimento Cheese
raw_recipe.description: This version of pimento cheese is sweetened with pickle relish. It is great as a sandwich, as a spread on crackers, or stuffed into celery.

review.reviewBody: At first i was never a member to this website because i would just print off the recipe and make it. When trying to leave a rating i realized i had to become a member so i did just to leave a rating to give Tom the credit that he well deserves for this recipe. I have always been a sweet pimento cheese lover. Its hard to find a good one on the internet. I dont understand why more people have not left ratings for this award winning cheese. Out of five stars i would rate this at least a 10+. Yes its that good. Thanks again Tom !!!!!!!

A delicious recipe! I only had 8 oz. cheddar, so that's what I used and it was fine. I've had authentic pimento cheese before and always felt they were just meh. This one is outstanding! Next time I'll add some jalapeno peppers to give it a sweet/hot flavor!
This is definitely my go to for pimento cheese. I might hot sauce occasionally.

4/7/19: Update: I ended up going back to this recipe, bc I felt like I did something wrong. I really liked the sweet relish the dish asked for, I use sweet salad cube bc they are bigger. I still did not add the sugar, relish is sweet enough. only 1/2 jar of pimentos, used garlic powder as well. Today I am making it for the 4th time. I also use extra sharp cheddar cheese and a good mayo.
This was amazing. Our friends and family agreed. I didn't change the ingredients, however i did put the cheese and pimentos in my food processor. Texture was perfect. Can't wait to make again.
This recipe had too much pickle relish for me but the rest of my family really liked it. I think I will half the amount of pickle relish and omit the pickle juice next time.

Gotta give props to Tom for the pickle relish idea, even though I didn't really follow the recipe. In fact, the cream cheese is the only thing I didn't change! I used shredded Moz (only cheese I had except velveeta), real mayo, homemade sweet/dill relish (dill pickles in the food processor with sweet pickle juice), jarred roasted red peppers (chopped to pimiento size), and left out the sugar. Oh, and I only made about half the recipe (didn't have much of the Moz...) and "eyeballed" all measurements. Wish I had some celery to try it on...

My granddaughter loves pimento cheese spread sandwiches and her talking about it always makes me hungry . I decided I would try to make my own. This recipe was very good. I let it in the refrigerator overnight. I took an ice cream scoop, kind of shaped it into a ball. Put it in a fancy little dish and served it with crackers for our family get-together on New Year's Day. Love the recipe, I made it just like it read.

I am like a connoisseur of pimento cheese. I love it. I buy it at the store all the time. I thought I would give this recipe a try so I could make it at home. My experience on this recipe was that it never turned yellow like the one in the store. The flavor was not there.I did use an offbrand sweet pickle relish instead of the one that I usually use by Vlasic. I could taste the difference in though pickle relish. That aside though this is not my favorite. I have enclosed a picture of both the store-bought and this recipe. The store-bought is on the left. You can see the difference. It also wasn’t sweet enough for me but that could have been the difference in the pickle relishes. I will try to again with the good pickle relish but still my never turned yellow and it wasn’t thick and creamy.
I made this with my own little added flare and it is by far better than any store or deli bought style.

Best I have ever made, I made pimento cheese for 40 years but this is the first time I've used cream cheese. This is a wonderful recipe, I'll make it again. 
Thanks to Tom!!
The BEST pimento cheese we've ever eaten! Thanks, Tom!
I love pimento cheese. Glad I found a recipe to make my own. It is great as a sandwich. I also just tried it with Frito scoops and it is awesome.

WOW! I am a pimento cheese convert. Never have been much of a fan, and when no choice but to eat it I've always leaned toward my mom's melted-Velveeta-and-mayo version more than the chunky style that everyone else makes. This version is ridiculously good; fluffy, a little bit sweet, and great addition of pickle and garlic. I agree with Dustin, surpised on the lack of ratings. Thanks Tom!
